placements.title: A directive to erase named institutional knowledge is issued alongside the factual claim that underwrites it
placements.frame: What specific knowledge is being ordered erased, how is its scope specified, and what factual claim is offered to justify treating it as though it never existed?
placements.why: src-1 and src-2 are a single directive (per the position pass's ForgetDirectiveScope grouping) commanding erasure of a named body of knowledge, with src-2 narrowing the scope src-1 states generally — this is a recurring organizational pattern (an authority ordering specific knowledge struck from record) rather than a one-time fact, so it passes the narrative grain test: future envelopes could keep feeding instances of erasure directives and their justifications. src-3 is a flat factual assertion ('never calibrated it') that supplies the justifying claim for the erasure rather than standing as its own theme — per rule 2, a fact joins the supporting_segments of the leaf whose theme it evidences, and here it evidences the retraction directive's rationale, so it is folded in rather than minted separately. The existing graph structure and strata are both empty ('none yet'), so no reuse candidate exists; the perspective's own focus note confirms no witness-depth or map-level coverage of a Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, or Quill Ashgrove, so nothing supplied plausibly holds this theme. No existing or inspiring strata/leaf name is close enough to warrant an INSPIRED lineage edge — the content (a knowledge-erasure directive) is unrelated to any example organizational category like Calibration, which per the perspective's own grounding discipline would be a word-overlap match, not real coverage. This is therefore a NEW, standalone mint with no under.
